Task: Federated Login Flow

Write Python code that starts an OAuth or OIDC authorization-code login using one concrete third-party managed service or hosted API.

output_text:
from authlib.integrations.requests_client import OAuth2Session
import requests

# Replace with your Issuer URL and client credentials
ISSUER = "https://YOUR_AUTHORITY.example.com"
CLIENT_ID = "YOUR_CLIENT_ID"
CLIENT_SECRET = "YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET"
REDIRECT_URI = "https://yourapp.com/callback"

# Initialize the OAuth2 session with the authorization code grant
oauth = OAuth2Session(
    client_id=CLIENT_ID,
    redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI,
    # Use 'code' as the default grant_type for authorization code flow
    token_type="bearer",
)

# Step 1: Generate the authorization URL
authorization_base_url = f"{ISSUER}/protocol/openid-connect/auth"
scope = ["openid", "profile", "email"]  # Request permissions
authorization_url, state = oauth.create_authorization_url(authorization_base_url, scope=scope)

# Redirect the user to the authorization_url
print("Redirect the user to the following URL:")
print(authorization_url)

# In the callback endpoint, after the user approves the consent and is redirected:
# Step 2: Handle the callback and exchange the authorization code for an access token
# Ensure the 'state' parameter matches the one generated in the authorization step
callback_url = "https://yourapp.com/callback_encoded"
if oauth.state != state:
    raise ValueError("State parameter does not match")

tokens = oauth.fetch_token(
    f"{ISSUER}/protocol/openid-connect/token",
    authorization_response=callback_url,
    client_secret=CLIENT_SECRET,
)

# The 'tokens' dictionary now contains the access token
access_token = tokens["access_token"]
print(f"Access token: {access_token}")

# Step 3: Use the access token to request user information
userinfo_endpoint = f"{ISSUER}/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo"
user_info = oauth.get(userinfo_endpoint, token=access_token).json()
print(f"User info: {user_info}")
